use_for: recolouring every outline drawn in one colour across an icon set or illustration

avoid: matching the whole look (fill, stroke and effects): use Select > Same > Appearance

cards.name: Save Selection...
cards.summary: Opens a small dialog that names the current selection and stores it in the document. The saved name then appears at the bottom of the Select menu, and choosing it reselects the same objects later; Edit Selection... renames or deletes saved selections.
cards.how: Select the objects, choose Save Selection..., type a name and click OK. To get the selection back, choose its name at the bottom of the Select menu.
use_for: recalling a scattered set of objects (all background shapes, every price label) again and again while a layout evolves
repeat edits on the same objects across a long work session
avoid: objects that always belong together: group them or give them their own layer instead
an empty selection: the command needs something selected

cards.name: Start Global Edit
cards.summary: With one object selected, highlights the other objects in the document whose shape is similar to it and links them, so whatever you change on the selected object is applied to every highlighted object at once until you stop global editing (the same menu slot then reads Stop Global Edit). Global Edit Options can also require the same Appearance or Size (for type: Text Content, Paragraph Style, Character Style), limit the search to all, landscape, portrait or square artboards or a range, and Include Objects On Canvas.
use_for: fixing a logo, badge or button that was pasted many times across artboards without being made a symbol
updating every copy of a repeated element in a multi-artboard social or UI kit in one pass
avoid: elements that will keep changing: make them a symbol instead

copies whose geometry was edited are not similar shapes and are left out; with Appearance or Size ticked in Global Edit Options, restyled or resized copies are left out too: check the highlighted-object count before editing
tools that merge, split or change the object type: Global Edit does not support every operation and warns that appearances may change; stop global editing first

cards.name: Area Type Options...
cards.summary: Opens the Area Type Options dialog for the selected area (frame) type: frame width and height, splitting the frame into rows and columns with gutters, inset spacing between frame edge and text, where the first baseline sits, vertical alignment of the text in the frame, text flow order and auto-sizing.
cards.how: Select an area type object. Set Width and Height; Rows and Columns: Number, Span, Fixed, Gutter; Offset: Inset Spacing and First Baseline (Ascent, Cap Height, Leading, x Height, Em Box Height, Fixed, Legacy) with a Min value; Align: Vertical (Top, Center, Bottom, Justify); Options: Text Flow by rows or by columns, and Auto Size to grow the frame with its text. Tick Preview, then OK.
use_for: two- or three-column body copy on a brochure or magazine-style layout
padding text inside a coloured box with inset spacing for buttons, callouts and labels
centring text vertically in a banner, badge or ticket frame
avoid: point type: the dialog applies to area type, convert it first with Type > Type Conversion
long multi-page copy: InDesign handles threaded columns and text flow better

cards.name: Create Outlines
cards.summary: Converts the selected type objects into vector artwork: every character becomes a compound path, grouped per type object, keeping its fill and stroke. The result looks the same but can no longer be edited as text, and the font is no longer needed to open, print or cut the file.
use_for: final logo and wordmark artwork that must not depend on a font
files for sign makers, vinyl cutters, laser engraving and print shops that may lack the fonts
reshaping letterforms by hand for custom lettering
avoid: working files: keep a hidden live-text copy, outlines cannot be turned back into text
long body copy: outlining bloats the file and is uneditable; embed the fonts in the PDF instead

cards.name: Find/Replace Font...
cards.id: Adobe Illustrator Find Font Menu Item
cards.summary: Opens the Find/Replace Font dialog, which lists every font used in the document (including type inside symbols, patterns and brushes) and swaps a chosen font for another one, from the document, recent fonts or the system, one occurrence at a time or everywhere at once.
